targets.summary: The same fix needs to go into foreach_tensor_norm_slow, the CPU/slow path, because right now only the CUDA path is fixed.
targets.adoption_evidence: The comment is attached to the top of the file (line 1, `#include <vector>`), so it applies to the whole file. For this file, the request was to add the same fix to `foreach_tensor_norm_slow`. Before the merge, that function just ran `result.emplace_back(at::linalg_vector_norm(t, ord, {}, false, dtype));` with no check. In the merged code, it works out `p` from `ord` once, before the loop. Inside the existing loop it then adds `if (p == std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()) { TORCH_CHECK(t.numel() > 0, "_foreach_norm cannot compute the infinity norm on an empty tensor ..."); }`. The merge also adds `#include <limits>` above `#include <vector>`. So the CPU/slow path now gets the empty-tensor infinity-norm check. It sits in the loop that was already there, so the list isn't walked an extra time, which fits point 1. This diff doesn't show whether `onlyCUDA` was removed from the test.
targets.stage3_reason: The PR added the empty-tensor infinity-norm check only on the CUDA path, so the CPU fallback `foreach_tensor_norm_slow` still called `at::linalg_vector_norm` with no guard, and CPU and CUDA behaved differently. The merged code adds `TORCH_CHECK(t.numel() > 0, "_foreach_norm cannot compute the infinity norm on an empty tensor...")` inside the slow path's existing loop, and a reviewer reading the whole PR could spot the missing CPU-side check.
